thesis: Rocket Lab is executing a credible transition from small-launch provider to end-to-end space company: record Q1 2026 revenue of $200.3M (+63.5% y/y), $2.2B backlog, its largest-ever launch contract (Neutron + Electron through 2029), and Space Systems now ~two-thirds of revenue. The +24% week reflects contract momentum and sector rotation. At ~$60B market cap (~75x annualized revenue), the price assumes Neutron succeeds on schedule and margins scale far beyond anything yet demonstrated.
catalysts: Neutron debut launch expected in 2026 - the single largest de-risking event
Largest contract in company history signed with confidential customer for Neutron and Electron through 2029 (May 2026)
$190M hypersonic test launch program with Anduril (US defense)
$2.2B backlog incl. 31 new Electron/HASTE contracts and five Neutron launch agreements (Q1 2026 results, May 2026)
Q2 2026 earnings (August 2026); continued US defense award flow
Mynaric and Motiv acquisitions expanding Space Systems capabilities
risk_factors: Neutron execution risk: any failure or slip in the debut is the dominant near-term risk to a stock priced for success
Valuation: ~$60B market cap on ~$800M annualized revenue (~75x sales), unprofitable; a 10% discount-rate DCF cannot approach the current price on demonstrated economics
Acquisition integration risk (Mynaric AG, Motiv Space Systems)
Sector sentiment whiplash: stock reacted to a Blue Origin test failure and anticipation of a SpaceX IPO, which could redirect capital away from RKLB
Beta 3.12 - drawdowns are violent; 5-day move of +24% cuts both ways
